learningObjective: Diagnose dynamic-shape performance regressions in compiled workloads from a mix of graph-break/recompile logs and per-shape latency data.

canonicalClaims.claim: Static-shape torch.compile produces one specialized graph per unique guard shape; first-time-seen shapes pay the JIT compile cost inside the request latency. Enabling dynamic shapes (dynamic=True or mark_dynamic) allows one graph to cover a range of shapes and eliminates repeated recompile spikes.
conditions: Request stream contains multiple distinct shapes.
nonImplications: Does not imply dynamic=True is free; guards and shape-generic kernels can add per-iteration overhead.
Does not imply larger cache_size_limit fixes the root cause; it merely hides evictions.

misconceptions.claim: Cache thrashing is the cause whenever recompiles are visible.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Thrashing requires eviction; with N unique shapes and cache_size_limit≥N there is no eviction.

misconceptions.claim: JIT compile cost is not part of request latency.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For first-time-seen shapes, compile time is charged to the request that triggered it.
A larger cache prevents evictions but does not remove first-time compilation cost.

misconceptions.claim: Dynamic shapes are always faster than static shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Static specialization can produce tighter kernels; dynamic generalization trades some peak throughput for shape flexibility.
